Mechanically the new step is fine: the PR body is passed through `env:` rather than interpolated into `run:` (avoids script injection), the job is gated on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` so `github.event.pull_request.body` is defined (empty body on `pull_request` types like `reopened` just skips the check), and `grep -P`/`\K`/herestrings all work in this job's bash (lp-bug-update.yaml already uses the same constructs). The blocking problem is semantic: the validation regex `LP:\s*\K[0-9]+` only accepts the legacy `LP: <digits>` form and rejects `LP: #<digits>` — the Launchpad-documented pattern is `LP: #<LP-Bug-Number>[, #<LP-Bug-Number>]...` (ubuntu.com/docs/launchpad/user/reference/comment-syntax), which the commit description explicitly says this change standardizes on. A PR body containing `Fixes LP: #12345` passes the outer keyword check and then hard-fails CI. Per the same docs, `LP: 123` without `#` is not a bug mention at all (`lp:` is the branch-prefix, expanding to `https://bugs.launchpad.net/+code/...`). The identical regex in `.github/workflows/lp-bug-update.yaml:24` is unchanged by this diff, so once references switch to the `#` form that workflow will silently stop extracting bug IDs — the two regexes must be updated (ideally shared) together. Also note the description promises a format switch and an LP-bug comment writer, neither of which is in this diff, and the CI gate validates the PR description while the LP updater parses commit messages, so the two surfaces can drift.

.github/workflows/ci.yaml.170: This comment documents a coupling that nothing enforces: the keyword regex is duplicated verbatim in `.github/workflows/lp-bug-update.yaml:24`, and this change is precisely about redefining the LP reference format — the two copies must be edited in lockstep or the CI gate and the Launchpad updater will disagree. Consider extracting the matching into a shared script (e.g. under `utilities/`) or a reusable composite action that both workflows call, instead of keeping the list in two places.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.171: Two validation gaps to be aware of: (1) grep matches line-by-line, so `.` never crosses a newline — the closing keyword and `LP:` must be on the same line; a body like a `## Fixes` heading followed by `LP: #123` on its own line skips the check entirely (and the same limitation means the launchpad updater misses it too). (2) The inner check on line 172 scans the whole body for any `LP:<digits>`, not the reference adjacent to the closing keyword, so `Closes LP: <malformed>` plus an unrelated `LP: 123` elsewhere still passes. If the intent is to validate the reference that follows the keyword, anchor both in a single regex rather than two independent greps. The trailing `\s*` here is also dead weight — `.*LP:` is equivalent for an unanchored grep match.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.172: Bug: this rejects the standard Launchpad format. `LP:\s*\K[0-9]+` requires digits immediately after `LP:` plus optional whitespace, so it matches `LP: 123456` but NOT `LP: #123456` — `#` is not whitespace, and grep's line-based matching can't skip past it. The Launchpad-documented pattern is `LP: #<LP-Bug-Number>[, #<LP-Bug-Number>]...` (ubuntu.com/docs/launchpad/user/reference/comment-syntax, 'Mention multiple Launchpad bugs'), i.e. the exact format this commit description says it is switching to. Consequence: a PR body containing `Fixes LP: #12345` passes the outer grep on line 171 and hard-fails here. If the `#` form is intended, use something like `LP:\s*#?\s*\K[0-9]+`, and update `.github/workflows/lp-bug-update.yaml:24` (identical regex, unchanged in this diff) in the same change — otherwise that workflow silently stops extracting bug IDs once references adopt `LP: #`.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.174: Make the failure actionable: `LP:<number>` shows neither the accepted whitespace/case variants (`LP:123`, `lp: 123` all pass) nor the documented `LP: #123456` form this change targets (which currently fails per the line-172 bug). Once the accepted syntax is settled, echo a concrete example of a passing line, e.g. `Expected syntax: Fixes LP: #123456`, so contributors can fix the description without guessing.
